solutionSearchEvidence: Current main already has the single durable-string adapter and previous-string rollback behavior from the earlier recovery path.
The remaining first-save failure leaves mismatched bytes when there is no previous string, so restoring absence must reuse caller storage rather than create a second save authority.
The same rollback boundary must cover a setItem exception that may occur after a partial mutation; otherwise verified-save failure can still corrupt the prior state.
Caller-supplied removeItem restores prior absence; when it is unavailable and the current bytes changed, rollback fails closed instead of claiming preservation.
